Nam lives in Hanoi. He works in a factory. Every morning he takes the bus at six. His shift starts at seven. In the evening he cooks dinner with his wife.
Nam has a small family. His wife is a nurse. They have a son and a daughter. The son is ten years old. The daughter is six. They also have a cat.
Yesterday Lan did not go to work. She visited her mother in the village. They cooked fish and rice. Lan went home at eight in the evening. She was tired but happy.
On Saturday Tom wakes up late. He drinks coffee and eats an egg. In the afternoon he plays soccer with his friends. In the evening he watches a movie.
It is seven o'clock. There are many people at the station. A train arrives and a train leaves. A woman buys a ticket. A boy eats a banana.
Our office is on the third floor. There are ten desks and two printers. The manager's room is next to the stairs. The kitchen is small but clean.

When I finished school, I wanted to work in a big city, but I had no experience. My uncle told me that a hotel in Da Nang needed a receptionist. I was afraid because my English was not very good, but I decided to try. On my first day, a guest from Australia asked me where he could rent a motorbike. I did not understand him, so I asked him to write it down. He smiled and wrote the word on a piece of paper.

After that, I began to study English for one hour every evening after work. I learned the words that guests used most often, and I practiced with the other receptionists. Six months later, I could answer most questions without help. The manager saw this and asked me to train two new workers. Today I am the head receptionist at that hotel. I still make mistakes, but I am no longer afraid to speak. My advice to young people is simple: do not wait until your English is perfect. Start using it now, and you will learn much faster.

Would you like to learn to cook Vietnamese food? The Community Center on Kim Ma Street has a new course this summer. The course starts on the eighth of July and finishes on the twenty-sixth of August. Classes are held every Saturday morning from nine to eleven thirty. Our teacher, Mrs Thu, worked as a chef in a large hotel for twenty years. Each class has no more than twelve students, so everyone gets help.

The course costs one hundred and fifty dollars. This includes all the food, but students must bring their own knife and an apron. To join, please fill in a form at the front desk before the first of July, or call Mr Binh. Students who finish the course will receive a small gift and a book of recipes.

Two years ago, I was always tired. I worked in an office for nine hours a day, I drove to work, and I usually ate fast food for lunch. When my doctor told me that I was heavier than I should be, I knew I had to change. I did not want to go to a gym because it was too expensive, so I started with small steps. First, I began to walk to work. It takes thirty minutes, and it is a nice way to start the day.

Next, I stopped buying lunch and started bringing rice and vegetables from home. That saved me about fifty dollars a month. I also went to bed one hour earlier. It was not easy at first, but I did not stop. After three months, I felt much better and I had lost five kilos. My wife saw the change and began to walk with me on Sundays. Now our children sometimes join us too. I am not perfect, and I still enjoy a cake on the weekend. But I have learned that a small change, if you keep doing it, can be better than a big plan that you never start.

The City Museum is looking for volunteers to help at its new exhibition about old Hanoi. The exhibition opens on the third of October and runs for six weeks. Volunteers work one day a week, on a Saturday or a Sunday, from ten o'clock until four. Your job is to welcome visitors and answer simple questions in English or Vietnamese. You do not need any experience, but you must be at least eighteen years old.

We give all volunteers a free lunch and a free ticket for one friend. Training is on the twenty-eighth of September at the museum. To apply, send an email to Ms Hanh before the fifteenth of September. Please tell us which day you prefer and why you want to help. Volunteers who help for all six weeks will also receive a letter of thanks from the museum.
